title: Choose the visual world
question: I’ve prepared two distinct directions for the redesign. Choose the one that feels right, or re-roll for another pair.

options.label: The Open Transcript
options.lineage: working call scripts and operator records
options.thesis: A real-feeling sample conversation becomes the page’s organizing surface.
options.viewport: One unboxed call transcript spans the first screen: oversized speaker turns, concise margin notes for disclosure and human handoff, and a clear link to discuss a call flow.
options.risk: If the transcript loses its rhythm, it can read like an ordinary chat interface.

raised.raise: Keep one continuous reading route across the whole page, so each section leads to the next without feeling like an isolated feature.
Show each call path stopping at an agreed action or a person, with boundaries visible in the example.
Label confirmed facts, examples, and project-specific unknowns distinctly, without implying a live monitoring system.
Keep one strong typographic hierarchy and let the main reading plane stay still while the page is read.
Give every turn a clear speaker and sequence number, so meaning never depends on color alone.
Preserve orientation as the page moves from the sample call to fit, implementation, support, and the next step.

options.label: The Call Route
options.lineage: telephone switching diagrams and route maps
options.thesis: One deliberate line traces what happens from hello to human follow-up.
options.viewport: The call route crosses the full opening screen rather than sitting in a panel: AI disclosure, approved intake, then a clearly labeled human branch. A direct project link sits at the route’s end.
options.risk: The route can resemble an operations dashboard if it implies real-time call data.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.thesis: Folded neighborhoods make separate call journeys feel connected.
options.viewport: A night map opens into several call journeys across a folded city.
options.case: The continuous page route is useful, but a dreaming city obscures the service and does not help a broad business audience identify their own calls.
options.kept: A continuous reading route across the page.
options.risk: Metaphor can bury the practical call path.

options.label: Glaze Path
options.lineage: ceramic kiln shelves and glaze runs
options.thesis: A controlled flow shows where an intake path stops or changes hands.
options.viewport: A call route flows from approved questions to a sharply marked stopping point or human fallback.
options.case: Clear stopping boundaries help, but molten glaze has little audience connection and makes product clarity depend on interpreting an abstract material.
options.kept: Every path must end at a clear, agreed next action.
options.risk: A flowing metaphor can make call steps harder to scan.

options.label: Night Instrument Panel
options.thesis: Every instrument owns one clearly labeled fact about a call.
options.viewport: A row of gauges represents a call route, project settings, and handoff state.
options.case: Clear labels would help, but a gauge cluster suggests continuous monitoring and live operational data that this service does not promise.
options.kept: Separate confirmed facts from project-specific unknowns.
options.risk: Can suggest live telemetry that is not established.

options.label: Signal Queue
options.thesis: Layered call lines reveal the next important turn first.
options.viewport: A dramatic field of dialogue layers makes the approved intake line the stable foreground.
options.case: A disciplined reading plane helps, but the retro text treatment is not a clear match for general business owners and the no-containment rule conflicts with dependable navigation and actions.
options.kept: A deliberate type hierarchy with a stable reading plane.
options.risk: Novelty can overpower the actual service.

options.label: Call Cards
options.thesis: Numbered caller turns make a sample conversation easy to follow.
options.viewport: A compact sequence of numbered cards shows caller and AI turns from greeting to follow-up.
options.case: Explicit speaker turns help, but game cards are a poor fit for owners evaluating a practical service and weaken the seriousness of human fallback.
options.kept: Number each turn and identify its speaker in text.
options.risk: The game metaphor could trivialize handoff decisions.

options.label: Ambient Console
options.thesis: Moving through rooms of stored call information makes the service feel spatial.
options.viewport: A dark three-dimensional room places the call sample beside connected sections for setup and support.
options.case: Spatial orientation is useful, but the console-room concept implies product software and configured live data rather than an implementation service.
options.kept: Keep section order easy to follow as the story progresses.
options.risk: A software-console metaphor could misstate what is being sold.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional software landing page explains the offer through a split hero and a row of feature cards.
canonCard.viewport: A polished category-default layout with headline and contact action opposite a generic call dashboard, followed by equal capability cards.
canonCard.risk: It is immediately familiar and easy to scan, but erases the service’s distinctive call handling proof.
